analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture illustrates Levels Beyond's Media to Cloud workflow. 1. A user uploads a video file to an S3 bucket (UserConsumerWeb -> S3). 2. S3 triggers Step Functions to orchestrate the workflow. 3. Step Functions invokes MediaConvert to generate a browser-friendly video proxy, while extracting technical metadata/checksums into DynamoDB. 4. Step Functions also triggers Rekognition (visual analysis/tagging) and Transcribe (audio-to-text conversion). 5. Rekognition writes timestamped tags directly to DynamoDB. 6. Transcribe writes transcriptions to DynamoDB and forwards text to Comprehend for NLP analysis (entity/profanity extraction). 7. Comprehend writes analysis results back to DynamoDB. 8. Finally, DynamoDB serves as a temporary store before data is ingested into Reach Engine (hosted on EC2 and EKS) for visualization and downstream orchestration.

analysis.step_by_step_reasoning:
The architecture diagram illustrates Sanofi's real-world evidence analytics platform (Arwen ecosystem) on AWS.
1. User Web Portal & Authentication: Static content is hosted on S3 and served via CloudFront (with SSL certificate). Users authenticate through Amazon Cognito federated with Sanofi SSO (ThirdParty).
2. Dynamic Traceability Logging: Dynamic requests pass from the web portal to API Gateway, which logs user activity and metadata in DynamoDB for full auditability.
3. Analytics Workspace Self-Service: Data scientists request self-service analytics environments via Service Catalog, which provisions dedicated RStudio on EC2 instances or SageMaker Notebooks (with chiffrated disks).
4. NLP Processing: User tasks trigger Lambda functions that utilize the AWS SDK to invoke Translate (batch translation) and Comprehend Medical (identification of medical entities).
5. Data Lake Storage: Isolated environments (EC2 RStudio, SageMaker) interact directly with user home buckets in the S3 Data Lake to ensure sensitive data remains securely inside the platform perimeter.

analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Cloud Health Secure State's real-time security monitoring and violations detection pipeline. 1. Security events from multiple cloud providers enter via UserCompanyDataStream into Kinesis Data Streams (Collect stage). 2. Collected assets are ingested into Amazon Neptune as graph data (handling 50M+ resources), and replicated/backed up to OpenSearch (Elasticsearch) and DynamoDB for search and analytical reporting. 3. Neptune and OpenSearch feed metrics to CloudWatch, which is monitored by a custom Shard Service to determine cluster capacity and adjust sharding dynamic routing back into the Collect Kinesis stream. 4. Events flow from the Collect stream to a Rules Kinesis stream, which executes rules against the Neptune graph model. Detected security violations are saved into DynamoDB and real-time alerts are dispatched to external notification services (Slack, Email, Splunk).
